target.name: Electric Sheep
target.founder: Gunjit Singh, Jarrett Herold, Naganand Murty

methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series A → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.0x) to $26M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 4 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Robotics & Manufacturing. Range: $1.1B - $2.0B.

data.narrative:
Electric Sheep, a Series A robotics and manufacturing company founded by Singh, Herold, and Murty, has raised $25.5M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comparable universe of nine robotics firms—one public (277810.KQ) and eight private—including peers at similar and adjacent stages: Generalist AI, Bedrock Robotics, Dexterity, and Walden Robotics.

Two triangulation methods apply. Stage-progression analysis uses the $25.5M total raised as a proxy base value and applies a 2.0x multiplier typical of Series A to next-stage advancement, implying a valuation of $51M. Peer-median analysis across four same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables yields a median valuation of $1.7B, with a range spanning $1.1B (Walden Robotics at Seed) to $2.0B (Generalist AI at Series B).

The two methods produce a wide implied range: $43M on the conservative end to $2.0B at the high end, with a median of $876M. The stage-progression method reflects Electric Sheep's early-stage position and limited historical capital deployment, while the peer-median approach captures the substantial valuations commanded by robotics specialists at proximate stages. The wide spread reflects material uncertainty around Electric Sheep's product maturity, market traction, and competitive positioning relative to named peers. Additional operational and market validation metrics would be required to narrow this band materially.
